label: the numerals twenty-one to one hundred
note: STAYS OPEN ON PURPOSE, and what is now covered is worth stating precisely. Chapter 104 teaches the SEVEN RUNGS from thirty to ninety -- tiis, chaaliis, pachaas, saath, sattar, assii, nabbe -- and chapter 79 teaches sau beside the rupee. That is every price, age and house number that LANDS ON a rung, including mock 2 reading item 4 (pachaas rupaye), which the old note named as unreadable. IT IS NOT THE WHOLE RANGE. Hindi does not build 21-99 from parts a learner can reassemble: pacciis is not paanch plus biis in any workable sense, and the seventy-two numbers between the rungs are each individually eroded and have to be met as words. The chapter says so rather than inventing a rule, and teaches the one thing that does hold -- HINDI PUTS THE SMALL NUMBER FIRST, so pacciis opens with the sound of paanch, the opposite of English. Probing this point on the rungs alone would claim a range the corpus does not teach; HL-C386 is the precedent for why that is not done. To close it honestly the track needs the in-between words themselves, which is a vocabulary tranche rather than a chapter.
